title: Fouling behaviour of pea protein isolate during ultrafiltration: comparison with whey protein at equivalent protein content

record.title: Fouling behaviour of pea protein isolate during ultrafiltration: comparison with whey protein at equivalent protein content
record.abstract: The fouling behaviour of pea protein isolate (PPI) solutions at 1, 3, and 6 g/L total protein was compared with that of whey protein isolate (WPI) at equivalent concentrations during ultrafiltration through 10 kDa polyethersulphone membranes at 2 bar TMP and 25 °C. PPI solutions exhibited 2.1-fold higher initial fouling rates than WPI at 6 g/L, attributed to the larger hydrodynamic diameter (122 nm vs. 18 nm, by dynamic light scattering) and broader size distribution of PPI aggregates. The cake compressibility index for PPI was 0.71 versus 0.54 for WPI. Alkaline CIP with 0.5% NaOH at 50 °C restored flux to 91% of initial for PPI-fouled membranes compared with 97% for WPI-fouled membranes, indicating a greater proportion of irreversibly adsorbed pea protein. Circular dichroism and intrinsic fluorescence confirmed that PPI contained higher levels of denatured globulin fractions contributing to irreversible adsorption. The study informs process design for plant-based protein ingredient manufacturing.
